name: Security audit & fix plan
description: Audit a scope for exploitable risks and turn the findings into a severity-ordered remediation plan. Read-only; nothing is changed until you choose to build.

config.instructions: Audit the security of the scope in workflow_input.request. workflow_input.context, when it is not empty, holds results from earlier in this conversation (for example findings or a plan the user has reviewed or edited): treat it as established input and build on it instead of repeating it, but check anything that looks stale against the workspace. Identify the assets and trust boundaries, then inspect input handling, authentication and authorization, secrets and sensitive data, filesystem, network, command and database boundaries, dependencies and configuration. Rank each finding by likelihood and impact, with evidence (file and symbol), an attack scenario and a specific remediation; separate confirmed findings from theoretical risks, and never print secrets. Do not modify files or run commands. The next step receives only your final message, not your tool history, so keep every fact it needs.

Turn workflow_input.request and the supplied findings into an actionable implementation plan for a fresh Build session that receives only your final message, not your exploration history. Order the remediation by severity and tie each step to a finding in workflow_input.audit. Verify the key facts in the code first, and preserve the user's requirements, decisions and relevant findings. Return ordered, numbered steps, each naming the files and symbols to change, the exact change and an observable acceptance check, followed by risks and prerequisites, with optional work clearly labeled as optional. Do not implement anything or claim anything was tested. Ask the user only for decisions you cannot resolve from the request or the code. Do not modify files or run commands. The next step receives only your final message, not your tool history, so keep every fact it needs.

route.when: The user asks whether code is secure, or wants vulnerabilities, risky dependencies, exposed secrets or unsafe configuration reviewed.
